LOG CABIN CON

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A builder sells dreams with impressive pics and plans, takes big deposits but fails to deliver a finish product while raking in hundreds of thousands of rands.

Unique Selling Point:
CROOK

Summary:
Meet Jan De Klerk – he’s has a couple of business names…. MMH Modular Homes, Pine Log Homes, Light Steel Homes – under all three he’s run the same kind of operation – overselling and under delivering from Brakpan to Kuruman.

We catch up with Jan de Klerk in an undercover sting operation.

Further information:
Jan de Klerk reels you in, takes your moolah and doesn’t deliver.

He’s lied about his membership to the Master Builders Asso. And The NHBRC. And his work is shoddy and not up to scratch.

Again it shows how consumers often bare the brunt of dodgy contractors – when the police are reluctant to take action, and a civil claim is expensive and often pointless because the money is usually long gone.

CASE STUDY 1 – JANICE FORSTER, JHB SOUTH
Janice Foster was quoted R200k for a log cabin – she paid R100k deposit. She got 21 holes dug and 13 wooden poles delivered – R4761 per hole! But Janice is no push over – she took Jan de Klerk to court and got a judgement against him. He was ordered by the court to refund Janice.

But the cash has not been forth coming. Jan has challenged the judgements – his reasoning is shocking and flawed. He argues that town planning regulations prevents any residential land owner building more than 40% of the plot – if that was the case – why quote, why take a deposit and why dig the holes? In addition he argues that he did at least R35k worth of work – even then that’s 21 holes dug by casual labour over 5 days at R7000 a day.

Janice has since repaired the damage to her garden at a cost of R81000. That’s over and about the R100k she paid Jan, and the legal fees she spent so far.

CASE STUDY 2 – VERONICA & FRIK ERASMUS
Frik took his pension money to build a log cabin in his children’s backyard. Frik has cancer and has not been well. He paid Jan de Klerk in full – R250k – he got a shell of a log cabin – the exterior walls and the steel frame, with parts of the roof – not floors, not fittings, not cupboards. The Eramus’ had to spend a further R150k to finish.

CASE STUDY 3 – SEDIBA ACADEMY – KURUMAN – NITA KUMM
In 2018, Jan de Klerk quoted R344k for the building a school classroom in Kuruman. He was paid the first payment of R60k for the deposit, the balance on completion. Although these aren’t his standard terms – he agreed and engaged with the client on whatsapp about the start of the project – if he had an issue with the deposit then – he would surely have raised before.

Nita managed to do some of her won digging and found that the money she paid had been spent. She also contacted AfriSki that confirmed they had no dealings with Jan de Klerk or his business – despite Jan sighting this as one of his projects.

CASE STUDY 4 – JOHAN VAN DER WESTHUIZEN
Oom Johan is old man. He was quoted R210k for the building of a log cabin, he ended up paying R225k and did not get a finished project – he is currently busy finalising it and has had to spend about an addition R200k to complete because there were issues with the workmanship.

Jan repeatedly lied to Oom Johan about the project and coming to site.

WHAT WE KNOW
Jan is not registered with the Master Builders Association.
Jan is not registered with the NHBRC.

Jan uses the same excuses, car trouble, labour trouble, the weather and will always need more cash.

Jan takes deposit, does minimal work and doesn’t finish the projects he was paid for.

UNDERCOVER
We do an undercover sting to get footage of Jan and get sales pitch. We use the same location for the bust.

INTERVIEWS
CASE STUDIES x 4
LEGAL EXPERT – JANUSZ LUTEREK – where do consumers stand – even with a judgement no joy.
NHBRC – confirming he is not registered and the legal implications
UNDERCOVER & CONFRONT WITH JAN

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: Choosing to renovate or extend a property is a huge decision - finding the right contractor is crucial.

LINK: Builders can be charming and convincing – they sell you a dream, but sometimes all you get is a nightmare project that leaves you out of pocket.

VO: Meet Jan de Klerk, the director of MMH Modular Homes. He sells log cabins and light steel frame homes – claiming to be a specialist in providing a complete turnkey solution. Crafting professionally done homes & log cabin structures that are technically flawless with amazing workmanship.

But these three clients beg to differ.

JOHAN: om eerlik te wees ek weet nie wat was reg nie, niks was reg nie /
ENGLISH: To be honest, I don’t know what was right, nothing was right.
JANICE: // I ended up with a garden with 21 holes // and one, one hell of an attitude from him.

VO: We sent in an operative with a hidden camera to get De Klerk’s sales pitch for ourselves.

JAN: The other guys will charge you a more or less the same, maybe a little less, but you won’t get this material

VO: Jan de Klerk talks a good game – promising expert workmanship and quick turn-around times.

JAN: at worst, let me tell you, worst case scenario… 2 months.

VO: But that’s not how it played out for the customers we spoke to.

Johan van der Westhuizen has been waiting for 9 months . The same goes for Janice Foster , who’s project also started in September 2020. But Nita Kumm takes the cake – she’s been waiting for more than two years.

In 2018, the Sediba Academy in Kuruman in the Northern Cape, contracted Jan de Klerk to build two classrooms, at a price tag of 310 thousand rand.

The project had to be completed by the 15th of November 2018 - it was a big expense for the school, but it was much needed according to Kumm.

NITA: Ons het het nie 50% deposito om te betaal nie ons het in die middel van november 2018 beskikbaar sal wees wat kan ek kom 60000 gee en hy het gesê hy sal 6000o aanvaar en die geld is toe in sy in sy rekening inbetaal
UPDATE STRAP ENGLISH:// I explained that we didn’t have 50% deposit to pay, we would only have money available mid-November 2018, that we would be able to pay the balance with, could I give him R60 000 and he said he’d be willing to accept R60 000.

VO: The deposit was paid mid-September . By the 15th of November 2018 – Jan was a no-show.

NITA: // elke keer as ek hom bel dan het hy verskoning gehad // hy’t vir my bly se hy is by Afriski in Lesotho
ENGLISH: Every time I called him, he’d have an excuse. //He kept telling me he was at Afriski in Lesotho and that’s why he can’t come because he’s building a three-storey building at Afriski.

VO: Afriski confirmed that no three-storey cabins were done in 2018 and that they had never heard of Jan de Klerk.

But that’s not the only thing he seems to have lied about.

On his website at the time , he displayed the logos of Master Builders of South Africa and the National Home Builders Registratio Council. He is not registered with either of the organisations . More recently, he only uses the NHBRC logo claiming that all his workers are registered .

LINK: Being registered with the NHBRC is not optional - in terms of legislations guiding the building industry, failure to register as a home builder is a criminal offence and can carry prison time or a fine.

VO: The NHBRC is a statutory body for the homebuilding industry. Craig Makapela checked their records for Jan de Klerk.

CRAIG: Jan de Klerk is not registered as a home builder.

VO: While there is record of an attempted NHBRC registration in 2016, it was never finalised .

CRAIG: I did not see him in any other form in our system as a competent person, but means as an engineer or a technical director, any other an entity in the system.

VO: Using the logos of industry bodies you are not affiliated to, is deceptive, alleges Attorney Janusz Luterek.

JANUSZ: You are making a representation in order to reel people in, // that in itself, to me is fraud, because you are using that as leverage in order to get the business.

VO: That’s why Janice Foster chose Jan de Klerk to build her a two-bedroom log cabin.

JANICE: his price was a bit higher than some of the other people that I'd gone to. But I took him because he was registered.

VO: Foster paid him a R100 000 deposit. In just under a month, she says only 21 holes were dug and 13 wooden poles delivered – that works out to a whopping R4761 per hole!

JANICE: //He would just come tell the guys know you've dug that hole in the wrong place, move it over, and then they would dig, spend the day digging. And then we hit a rock.

VO: De Klerk now needed to hire a jackhammer – and he wanted Foster to pay for it . Foster refused – realising she was being taken for a ride, she halted the project.

Luterek says Foster was within her rights.

JANUSZ: //he can't be asking for more money now. The deposit he received hasn't been accounted for. // You wouldn't pay somebody more money // that's clearly non performing //

VO: Sediba Academy got absolutely nothing for the R60 000 deposit.

NITA: // heel aan die einde toe sy vir my maar se terme is duidelik 50% 30% 20% //en dis hoekom hy kan nie hy kan nie werk nie .

JANUSZ: // at the time he took the 60 thousand, it wasn't a problem. It became a problem. He manufactured the problem at the end in order to explain why he didn't do what he was supposed to do.

VO: Johan van der Westhuizen was quoted for a carport and a complete light steel structure including foundations and fittings , but that’s not what he got.

VO: According to Van Der Westhuizen a final payment of R62 000 was still outstanding, Jan De Klerk had already been paid R225 000 - but the project was far from finished .

LINK He delivered just a wooden frame and some log cladding - no windows, no roof, no floor.

VO: The carport is just a frame. Van der Westhuizen says even De Klerk was unimpressed with his own work.

JOHAN: // I said to him will you be happy if you pay all that money for this kind of work. And he word to me no, i know you we take you for a ride, but we are gonna fix it in the next week or so.

VO: But that never happened . Van der Westhuizen regrets falling for De Klerk’s empty promises.

JOHAN: /soos hy vir my gesê het in sy eie woorde hy is 'n afrikaner ,ek is afrikaner hy sal my nooit in doen nie, hy’s 'n christen hy gaan kerk toe M16 //een van sy werkers het vir my gesê hulle werk net tot waar die ruite in gaan, windows, dan sien jy hulle nie weer nie en dit het gebeur
ENGLISH: He said to me in his own words, that he is an Afrikaner, I am an Afrikaner - he will never do me in, he is a Christian, he goes to church. One of his workers told me, they only work up to the windows, then you won’t see them again. And that’s what happened!

VO: By Van der Westhuizen’s estimations, It’s costing at least another R200 000 to finish De Klerk attempt at a log cabin.

Kwaaitjie Weyers has taken over the project .

MAC: What you found here was 225000, rand?
KWAAITJIE: // the materials that was left, maybe 110 thousands , 100 thousands, nothing more.
MAC: Yeah. And the work that was done,
KWAAITJIE: I won't I won't even say twenty thousand
MAC: Do you think he’s con?
KWAAITJIE: Definitely, definitely.

VO: It was time to get some answers from De Klerk. We interrupted his meeting with our undercover operative.

MAC: Jan de klerk? how you? My name is Mac Moleili from Carte Blanche – I have some questions regarding projects?
JAN: What project?
MAC: The project that you did with the Janice, another one,…
JAN: WHO?

VO: It seems that Jan de Klerk had sudden memory loss.

JAN: I say nothing ok [walks off]//

VO: De Klerk got in his car and sped off.

UPSOUND….. What about these people’s money?

VO: We followed up with a call. He insists there are two sides to a story.

MAC: Will you meet with us?
JAN: I will meet but I’ll be be honest with you, if there's any cameras, I walk away
MAC: but we from Carte BLAnche, we work with cameras.

VO: De Klerk opted to send a letter from his attorneys - it stated that De Klerk’s livelihood has been greatly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and he is attempting “to settle any disputes in an amicable fashion.”

De Klerk confirmed he is not registered with the Master Builders Association, claiming he was defrauded by a third party assisting with the registration process.

With Regards to the NHBRC, he claims he is not required to be registered, because he doesn’t partake in the building and stated that all his workers are registered, as displayed on his website.

Makapela says this statement doesn’t hold water .

CRAIG: it's his entity that's supposed to be registered with the NHBRC and then then from there you employ people under your company.

VO: The names of De Klerk’s so-called registered workers were not forthcoming .

While no specific mention is made of Kumm and Van der Westhuizen, De Klerk declined to comment on Foster’ s case, citing that there were legal proceedings under way.

Foster managed to get a default judgment against De Klerk. He is currently trying to have it rescinded. Luterek has reviewed De Klerk’s affidavit - in it he claims his project costs were R35 400.

JANUSZ: But that is much, much less than the deposit he received. So even if what he says is true, you should still refund the people the balance of the deposit.

VO: Having lost a R100 000 to De Klerk and spent an additional R80 000 on legal fees - Foster is even more out of pocket and disillusioned by the system.

JANICE: These guys get away with it, // they go out and take a certain amount from you. They know it's pointless trying to go to the law to get that back


JANUSZ: So the question is//where is the rest of the money he collected? Is all the deposits now if he used that money for other purposes, that, in fact, there might be a criminal investigation into that.

VO: It’s cold comfort for the clients who are out of pocket.

MAC: What say
NITA: hoe kry jy die nag geslaap om blatant net so te steel en nou net aangaan met jou lewe en net nog mense te besteel.



PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: A log cabin contractor rakes in hundreds of thousands in deposits but fails to finish projects – we catch up with the man that’s been overselling and underdelivering from Brakpan to Kuruman.

PROMO 2
VO: A log cabin contractor promises to build dream homes, but comes up short delivering unfinished nightmare projects - we meet the culprit who's left clients out of pocket from Brakpan to Kuruman.

PROMO 3
VO: We track down a Gauteng log cabin builder that has duped clients out of hard-earned cash – leaving unfinished projects from Brakpan to Kuruman - his workmanship is shoddy and his clients are furious.

VO: But that never happened . Van der Westhuizen regrets falling for De Klerk’s empty promises. JOHAN: /soos hy vir my gesê het in sy eie woorde hy is 'n afrikaner ,ek is afrikaner hy sal my nooit in doen nie, hy’s 'n christen hy gaan kerk toe M16 //een van sy werkers het vir my gesê hulle werk net tot waar die ruite in gaan, windows, dan sien jy hulle nie weer nie en dit het gebeur ENGLISH: He said to me in his own words, that he is an Afrikaner, I am an Afrikaner - he will never do me in, he is a Christian, he goes to church. One of his workers told me, they only work up to the windows, then you won’t see them again. And that’s what happened! VO: By Van der Westhuizen’s estimations, It’s costing at least another R200 000 to finish De Klerk attempt at a log cabin. Kwaaitjie Weyers has taken over the project . MAC: What you found here was 225000, rand? KWAAITJIE: // the materials that was left, maybe 110 thousands , 100 thousands, nothing more. MAC: Yeah. And the work that was done, KWAAITJIE: I won't I won't even say twenty thousand MAC: Do you think he’s con? KWAAITJIE: Definitely, definitely. VO: It was time to get some answers from De Klerk. We interrupted his meeting with our undercover operative. MAC: Jan de klerk? how you? My name is Mac Moleili from Carte Blanche – I have some questions regarding projects? JAN: What project? MAC: The project that you did with the Janice, another one,… JAN: WHO? VO: It seems that Jan de Klerk had sudden memory loss. JAN: I say nothing ok [walks off]// VO: De Klerk got in his car and sped off. UPSOUND….. What about these people’s money? VO: We followed up with a call. He insists there are two sides to a story. MAC: Will you meet with us? JAN: I will meet but I’ll be be honest with you, if there's any cameras, I walk away MAC: but we from Carte BLAnche, we work with cameras. VO: De Klerk opted to send a letter from his attorneys - it stated that De Klerk’s livelihood has been greatly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic and he is attempting “to settle any disputes in an amicable fashion.” De Klerk confirmed he is not registered with the Master Builders Association, claiming he was defrauded by a third party assisting with the registration process. With Regards to the NHBRC, he claims he is not required to be registered, because he doesn’t partake in the building and stated that all his workers are registered, as displayed on his website. Makapela says this statement doesn’t hold water . CRAIG: it's his entity that's supposed to be registered with the NHBRC and then then from there you employ people under your company. VO: The names of De Klerk’s so-called registered workers were not forthcoming . While no specific mention is made of Kumm and Van der Westhuizen, De Klerk declined to comment on Foster’ s case, citing that there were legal proceedings under way. Foster managed to get a default judgment against De Klerk. He is currently trying to have it rescinded. Luterek has reviewed De Klerk’s affidavit - in it he claims his project costs were R35 400. JANUSZ: But that is much, much less than the deposit he received. So even if what he says is true, you should still refund the people the balance of the deposit. VO: Having lost a R100 000 to De Klerk and spent an additional R80 000 on legal fees - Foster is even more out of pocket and disillusioned by the system. JANICE: These guys get away with it, // they go out and take a certain amount from you. They know it's pointless trying to go to the law to get that back JANUSZ: So the question is//where is the rest of the money he collected? Is all the deposits now if he used that money for other purposes, that, in fact, there might be a criminal investigation into that. VO: It’s cold comfort for the clients who are out of pocket. MAC: What say NITA: hoe kry jy die nag geslaap om blatant net so te steel en nou net aangaan met jou lewe en net nog mense te besteel. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: A log cabin contractor rakes in hundreds of thousands in deposits but fails to finish projects – we catch up with the man that’s been overselling and underdelivering from Brakpan to Kuruman. PROMO 2 VO: A log cabin contractor promises to build dream homes, but comes up short delivering unfinished nightmare projects - we meet the culprit who's left clients out of pocket from Brakpan to Kuruman. PROMO 3 VO: We track down a Gauteng log cabin builder that has duped clients out of hard-earned cash – leaving unfinished projects from Brakpan to Kuruman - his workmanship is shoddy and his clients are furious.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A builder sells dreams with impressive pics and plans, takes big deposits but fails to deliver a finish product while raking in hundreds of thousands of rands.
metadata.Summary: Meet Jan De Klerk – he’s has a couple of business names…. MMH Modular Homes, Pine Log Homes, Light Steel Homes – under all three he’s run the same kind of operation – overselling and under delivering from Brakpan to Kuruman. We catch up with Jan de Klerk in an undercover sting operation.
metadata.Further information: Jan de Klerk reels you in, takes your moolah and doesn’t deliver. He’s lied about his membership to the Master Builders Asso. And The NHBRC. And his work is shoddy and not up to scratch. Again it shows how consumers often bare the brunt of dodgy contractors – when the police are reluctant to take action, and a civil claim is expensive and often pointless because the money is usually long gone. CASE STUDY 1 – JANICE FORSTER, JHB SOUTH Janice Foster was quoted R200k for a log cabin – she paid R100k deposit. She got 21 holes dug and 13 wooden poles delivered – R4761 per hole! But Janice is no push over – she took Jan de Klerk to court and got a judgement against him. He was ordered by the court to refund Janice. But the cash has not been forth coming. Jan has challenged the judgements – his reasoning is shocking and flawed. He argues that town planning regulations prevents any residential land owner building more than 40% of the plot – if that was the case – why quote, why take a deposit and why dig the holes? In addition he argues that he did at least R35k worth of work – even then that’s 21 holes dug by casual labour over 5 days at R7000 a day. Janice has since repaired the damage to her garden at a cost of R81000. That’s over and about the R100k she paid Jan, and the legal fees she spent so far. CASE STUDY 2 – VERONICA & FRIK ERASMUS Frik took his pension money to build a log cabin in his children’s backyard. Frik has cancer and has not been well. He paid Jan de Klerk in full – R250k – he got a shell of a log cabin – the exterior walls and the steel frame, with parts of the roof – not floors, not fittings, not cupboards. The Eramus’ had to spend a further R150k to finish. CASE STUDY 3 – SEDIBA ACADEMY – KURUMAN – NITA KUMM In 2018, Jan de Klerk quoted R344k for the building a school classroom in Kuruman. He was paid the first payment of R60k for the deposit, the balance on completion. Although these aren’t his standard terms – he agreed and engaged with the client on whatsapp about the start of the project – if he had an issue with the deposit then – he would surely have raised before. Nita managed to do some of her won digging and found that the money she paid had been spent. She also contacted AfriSki that confirmed they had no dealings with Jan de Klerk or his business – despite Jan sighting this as one of his projects. CASE STUDY 4 – JOHAN VAN DER WESTHUIZEN Oom Johan is old man. He was quoted R210k for the building of a log cabin, he ended up paying R225k and did not get a finished project – he is currently busy finalising it and has had to spend about an addition R200k to complete because there were issues with the workmanship. Jan repeatedly lied to Oom Johan about the project and coming to site. WHAT WE KNOW Jan is not registered with the Master Builders Association. Jan is not registered with the NHBRC. Jan uses the same excuses, car trouble, labour trouble, the weather and will always need more cash. Jan takes deposit, does minimal work and doesn’t finish the projects he was paid for. UNDERCOVER We do an undercover sting to get footage of Jan and get sales pitch. We use the same location for the bust. INTERVIEWS CASE STUDIES x 4 LEGAL EXPERT – JANUSZ LUTEREK – where do consumers stand – even with a judgement no joy. NHBRC – confirming he is not registered and the legal implications UNDERCOVER & CONFRONT WITH JAN
